blocks.text: The Standard Model is the collection of theories that describe the smallest experimentally observed particles of matter and the interactions between energy and matter. Three categories of particles form the Standard Model (Fig. 12.8): quarks, leptons and the bosons. Matter, which makes up only about 5% of the universe, is composed of quarks and leptons. The fundamental bosons provide three forces: electromagnetism, the strong nuclear force and the weak nuclear force. The Higgs boson, discovered in 2012, explains how the other particles get mass.

blocks.title: Limits of the Standard Model
blocks.text: The model is still considered incomplete. Currently it is unable to explain many important features of the known universe, such as (i) gravity, (ii) dark matter (27% of the universe) and (iii) dark energy (68% of the universe).

blocks.prompt: Describe the classification of elementary particles (comprehensive question 12.8). The electroweak theory was introduced by whom (MCQ 12.15)?
blocks.explanation: In the Standard Model the elementary particles are fermions, which make up matter, and bosons, which carry forces. The fermions are six quarks (up, down, charm, strange, top, bottom), which combine into hadrons (baryons of three quarks, mesons of a quark and an antiquark), and six leptons (electron, muon, tau and their neutrinos); each has an antiparticle. The bosons are the photon, the gluons, the W and Z, and the Higgs boson. The electroweak theory, uniting the electromagnetic and weak forces, was developed by Dr. Abdus Salam with Glashow and Weinberg (Nobel Prize 1979): option (d).

items: Standard Model: quarks and leptons (matter, about 5% of the universe) and bosons carrying the electromagnetic, strong and weak forces; the Higgs boson (2012) explains mass. It cannot yet explain gravity, dark matter (27%) or dark energy (68%).
